preservation_map.claim: Tenant onboarding is a cross-team operation. An application needs frontend assets, backend routing, EMS2 entitlements, and portal catalog records before it can appear and launch for a tenant. The topic connects the [[entities/admin-module]], frontend and backend onboarding, schema and routing material, the SSDR entitlement discussion, and user-stated access rules.

preservation_map.claim: The admin manual describes three functions in the application catalog: Module Mapping, Drawer Category, and Tile Configuration. A module mapping links an import-map module name to an asset path; users enter the name without `@fm/` or spaces, and the active import-map API adds `@fm/` automatically. A drawer category groups tiles. A tile configuration record stores display details, container and route information, and entitlement configuration. Module and tile paths must match routing paths and are entered without a leading slash or spaces. Comma-separated role entities are converted into an array by the API. These functions and their relationships are collected in [[concepts/admin-catalog-configuration]] and [[concepts/portal-tile-workspace-model]].
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The manual defines a [[concepts/maker-checker-verification-workflow]]: creation or modification produces an `un-verified` record; a different user checks and verifies it before activation. Deactivation returns a verified record to `un-verified`. Each admin function keeps its own audit history. The supplied text does not fully specify rollback, activation propagation, or concurrent edits.
preservation_map.note: Full paragraph preserved or source-version label updated.

preservation_map.claim: The 12 November clarification allows a portal administrator to read every tenant's audit history and configuration. A tile must never reference metadata from another tile, including when an administrator submits its configuration. Cross-tenant write and verification permissions, the classification of tile metadata, and rules for shared tenant records remain open. preservation_map.claim: [[concepts/frontend-onboarding]] spans frontend and backend work. The development principle assigns portal-backend availability to the microfrontend team and each application's backend availability to its application team, an [[concepts/application-ownership]] split. Application teams choose their deployment approach and provide static-file and API URLs for NGINX configuration. The frontend procedure starts from separate container and tile templates, updates names, webpack, interfaces, entry points, tests, and the local import map, then links application registration through the admin manual. The backend procedure collects application URLs for proxy and CORS configuration, requires EMS2 role or entitlement setup, and directs services to SDK-based JWT validation and entitlement integration.

preservation_map.claim: The explicit user clarification permits tile visibility and launch through one configured EMS2 entity when the tile's subject setting is empty. The user must still satisfy portal-entry requirements and hold entitlement for that entity. The owner and scope answer identifies [[entities/portal-team]] across local, test, UAT, and production. This decision has approval pending. It resolves only the single-entity, empty-subject scope; it does not select a multiple-entity matching rule or an SSDR delegation option. The measurable result is defined in [UI-EMPTY-SUBJECT-AC-001](../../../records/candidates/security/KT-sdk-and-entitlements.md#ui-empty-subject-ac-001). See [[concepts/portal-entry-and-tile-authorization]].

preservation_map.claim: The SSDR discussion describes report and download users with different EMS2 entity assignments. It proposes multiple tile entities and optional subject checks for selected tenants; an empty subject would skip validation under that proposal. It also considers adding missing EMS2 assignments or delegating authorization to SSDR. The temporary guest-access approach is struck through. The discussion states that the portal does not implement entitlement control outside existing systems such as EMS2. These are alternatives, not an approved bypass or deployed permission rule.
